```text
the flop. This texture is also a little
wetter and less favourable for his BU
opening range, which might contain
every offsuit A, but certainly not every

ups, giving Hero a big boost of fold
equity on the turn. Betting this turn is
therefore mandatory. Hero cannot
```

## PDF page 1307

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/grinders%20manual.pdf#page=1307)

```text
Well, 8x is a very small part of his
range. There aren't too many combos of
that in a tighter player's pre-flop opening
range even from the BU. The bulk of his
turn calling range then will consist of
stuff that wasn't overly happy on the flop
and was probably giving up on most
turns but likes this one enough to call.
The hands I'm referring to are those with
one high club, usually the Ac or Kc. This
means that Hero has a clear plan
available. He should be happy to
continue his bluff on blank rivers as
these hands have now bricked and are
just A-high or K-high facing a second
bet from an uncapped range. They'll
almost always be folding. On a club
river, however, Hero should be inclined
```

```text
The upshot is that checking is the only

catch all of Villain's delayed c-bet bluffs
this way and keep our checking twice
range a bit stronger. Hero definitely
needs a more polarised betting range on
this turn than betting TT would create.

Some students may argue that our hand
has a flush draw and this is a reason to
bet. It's not. All that the flush draw does
is allow us to check/call even more
happily as we mind less river cards. It
doesn't make us more inclined to bet.
```
